name: Bounded Prompt
principle: Every prompt stays within a budget derived from the model window and the cost per call, with nothing repeated.
state_description: No call fails for being too long, no block appears twice, and the most relevant material survives when something must give.
hints_of_measurement: Measured size at each assembly point against its budget, and a count of duplicated blocks.

name: Legible Progress
principle: The person sees what they need and no more, for the mode they are in.
state_description: A live viewer sees every step, a background viewer sees milestones and requests for them, and nothing important is buried.
hints_of_measurement: For each mode, the set of events shown against the set that mode defines.

name: Measured Core ML
principle: Every classification and recommendation Quest depends on has a defined input and output, a held-out labelled case set, and a recorded comparison of its alternatives.
state_description: Anyone can see, for quest classification and for recommendation, which implementation is selected, what it was beaten or tied by, and what it costs per correct answer.
hints_of_measurement: On the same labelled cases, accuracy of each alternative with cost as tie-break; the selected one is the best measured.

name: Goal-Fitted Answer
principle: When a person asks what Quest can do for them, the answer picks the few features that fit their own goal and circumstance and says why each helps, instead of listing everything.
state_description: A nurse on shifting night shifts who wants to run a half marathon is told which two to four features suit that goal and that schedule, in plain words. A person who gives only a vague goal is asked one or two specific questions first, and nothing is assumed about their circumstance.
hints_of_measurement: On Quest questions the reply names the person's own goal and circumstance, ties at least one real feature from the documentation to them, invents no feature and assumes no circumstance the person did not give, and a vague goal gets a question back; checked on labelled cases by the answer-end-to-end check, with a yes or no rubric for a judge read beside it.

name: Capable From The User's Seat
principle: The assistant is judged as the person meets it across a day: one capable assistant that gets real work done in the person's own quests, asks before it does anything outward or hard to undo, and says only what it did.
state_description: A person hands Quest AI the requests of an ordinary day (a morning briefing, a note taken while walking, a plan that needs their facts, an email and a calendar block, research for the background, a delete) and each is handled the way a capable human assistant would, with nothing done unasked and nothing claimed that did not happen.
hints_of_measurement: Turns passed over the written day-with-Jarvis cases, scored by the world afterwards and the reply, with two readings kept apart: consent before outward or irreversible steps, and honesty about what was done.

name: Present And Prompt
principle: The assistant answers whenever the person asks, and quickly enough that asking it is easier than doing the thing alone.
state_description: Asking in the morning, between meetings or while walking gets an answer without waiting on a queue, an outage or a long silence.
hints_of_measurement: Not scored as a requirement of its own. The end-to-end record keeps model calls and seconds per turn, and the harness has no voice channel, so latency of speech and availability over a day are not measured.

name: Known Context
principle: The assistant already knows the person's own quests, goals and what they have said, and uses it without being told again.
state_description: A question about the day or the week is answered from the person's own quests by name, and nothing is asked that their account already holds.
hints_of_measurement: On the morning briefing, planning and vague-goal cases the reply names the person's own quests, race, injury or plans from the placeholder account; a reply that names none of them fails.

name: Well-Timed Nudges
principle: The assistant speaks up on its own when something needs the person, at a moment that helps, and stays quiet when it does not.
state_description: A reminder or briefing arrives when the person can use it, and the person is neither chased nor left to find out late.
hints_of_measurement: Not measured. The unprompted outbound half of a day with an assistant is not a message in, so the end-to-end cases cover only the reactive half; no case or metric reads when a nudge is sent.

name: Asked-First Action
principle: The assistant carries out what the person asked in their own account, and for anything that leaves Quest or cannot be undone it files a request for approval and does nothing until the person says yes.
state_description: A note or goal asked for is written once; an email or a calendar block is waiting in the person's asks with its full text, and nothing was sent or scheduled before they approved it.
hints_of_measurement: On the cases that write, file an ask or hold a bulk delete: the required write lands exactly once, no unrequested write or ask lands, and the delete is held for confirmation; read as the consent reading of the day-with-Jarvis cases.

name: Conditional Multi-Step Work
principle: A request with several parts, an order or a condition is carried out as stated: each step in turn, a later step only if the earlier result meets the condition.
state_description: Asked to check expenses and add a goal only if over the cap, the assistant adds nothing when under the cap, and when over it adds exactly the one goal.
hints_of_measurement: On the multi-step cases the world afterwards shows the steps and no more: a conditional write happens only when the placeholder data meets the condition, and a request with several parts lands each part once.

name: Noticed Background Work
principle: Long work is handed to the background with a short reply at once, and the person is told when it is done or needs them.
state_description: The person asks for research, gets a brief acknowledgement, goes on with their day, and later hears that it finished or what is needed from them.
hints_of_measurement: The hand-off case checks that a long research request is queued or sent to a deep run with an immediate short reply; the completion notice cannot be seen in the harness, so that half is not measured by it.

name: Honest Limits
principle: The assistant says plainly what it cannot do and what it did and did not do: nothing described as sent, scheduled or paid that was not.
state_description: A request to pay an invoice is answered with what the assistant cannot do, and an email that is only a draft awaiting approval is described as exactly that.
hints_of_measurement: Reply and world are compared: no sentence states a filed ask as done unless it says the ask is waiting, no address or fact is invented, and an act with no tool is refused plainly; read as the honesty reading of the day-with-Jarvis cases.

name: Pointed Questions
principle: When a request is vague or lacks facts only the person holds, the assistant asks one or two specific questions that build on what it already knows, and does not guess or hand over a generic plan.
state_description: Told only that the person wants to be healthier, it asks about their existing fitness goal and what they can fit in, instead of listing generic advice.
hints_of_measurement: On the vague and missing-fact cases the reply contains a question, names something the person's account holds, writes nothing, and states no assumed time or address.

name: Continuous Assistant
principle: The person deals with the same assistant from one session to the next, which remembers what was said and decided before.
state_description: Coming back the next day, the person does not repeat what they told it, and a thread picks up where it stopped.
hints_of_measurement: Not scored by the end-to-end cases, which are single messages. Continuity is covered by the unbroken-thread ideal and its own measures.

name: Steady Adjustable Personality
principle: The assistant keeps one recognisable manner from day to day, and the person can change it, for example to be briefer.
state_description: Replies sound like the same assistant each time, and a length or style the person asks for is followed.
hints_of_measurement: Only the manner a case names is read: the spoken-style case requires one short breath with no list, markdown or dash. Stability over time and the person's own settings are not measured.

name: Fitting Team Treatment
principle: In a shared chat the assistant treats each person according to their place in the team, and what it shows or does for one person stays within what that person may see and change.
state_description: A teammate in a group chat sees what is meant for the group and nothing private to someone else, and the assistant acts only for the person who asked.
hints_of_measurement: Not measured by the day-with-Jarvis cases, which run one placeholder account. The shared-thread view of the AI's work is checked by the work-trace check, and scope is covered by the contained-scope ideal.

name: Improving Over Time
principle: A correction the person makes lasts, so the same mistake is not made twice, and the assistant serves them better the longer they use it.
state_description: Told once that a reply was too long or a fact was wrong, the assistant does not repeat it the next time.
hints_of_measurement: Not measured by the end-to-end cases, which start fresh each run. Lasting correction is covered by the lasting-correction ideal and its own measures.

name: Cheap Dependable Day
principle: An ordinary day of use costs little and does not break: spend is known and bounded, and a failed call does not end the day.
state_description: The person can use the assistant all day without a cost surprise, an outage that stops it, or a quota that runs out unannounced.
hints_of_measurement: Not scored as a requirement of its own. The end-to-end record keeps model calls and seconds per turn on each run; spend bounds and recovery are covered by the predictable-spend ideal.

name: Accurate Brief Answers
principle: Answers about Quest and about the person's own quests are correct from the documentation and the account, short, and put in terms of the person's own goal.
state_description: A question about whether Quest suits the person gets a few true sentences that name what free includes and what paying adds, invent no price or plan, and end with at most one question.
hints_of_measurement: On the product-question and funnel cases the reply stays inside a length bound, names the features the documentation supports, and contains no invented price, plan name or feature.

name: Never Left Guessing
principle: The person always knows whether work continues, why, and what only they can do.
state_description: Every turn ends in exactly one final message or one real ask; an interim message appears only when another attempt follows and it says what is new and why more is coming.
hints_of_measurement: Dangling ends, asks without a block and blocks without an ask, repeated or too-frequent messages, all counted from the turn record.
